# PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE] Contents of this Part

## Part not to apply where claimant uses Part 8 procedure

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Part not to apply where claimant uses Part 8 procedure] 16.1 This Part does not apply where the claimant uses the procedure set out in Part 8 (alternative procedure for claims).

## Contents of the claim form

## 16.2

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (1) The claim form must –

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (a) contain a concise statement of the nature of the claim;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (b) specify the remedy which the claimant seeks;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (c) contain a statement of value in accordance with rule 16.3, where the claimant is making a claim for money;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (d) contain a statement of the interest accrued on that sum, where the only claim is for a specified sum; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (e) contain such other matters as may be set out in a practice direction.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (1A) In civil proceedings against the Crown, as defined in rule 66.1(2), the claim form must also contain –

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (a) the names of the government departments and officers of the Crown concerned; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (b) brief details of the circumstances in which it is alleged that the liability of the Crown arose.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (1A1) In a claim to which Part 45 does not apply, no amount shall be entered on the claim form for the charges of the claimant’s legal representative, but the words ‘to be assessed’ shall be inserted.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (2) If the particulars of claim specified in rule 16.4 are not contained in, or are not served with the claim form, the claimant must state on the claim form that the particulars of claim will follow.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (3) If the claimant is claiming in a representative capacity, the claim form must state what that capacity is.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (4) If the defendant is sued in a representative capacity, the claim form must state what that capacity is.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (5) The court may grant any remedy to which the claimant is entitled, even if that remedy is not specified in the claim form.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.2] (Part 22 requires a claim form to be verified by a statement of truth)

## Statement of value to be included in the claim form

## 16.3

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (1) This rule applies where the claimant is making a claim for money.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (2) The claimant must, in the claim form, state –

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (a) the amount of money claimed;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (b) that the claimant expects to recover –

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (i) not more than £10,000; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (ii) more than £10,000 but not more than £25,000; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (iii) more than £25,000 but not more than £100,000; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (iv) more than £100,000; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (c) that the claimant cannot say how much is likely to be recovered.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (3) Subject to paragraph (3A) and (3AA), in a claim for personal injuries, the claimant must also state in the claim form whether the amount which they expect to recover as general damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenity is –

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (a) not more than £1,500; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (b) more than £1,500.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (3A) Where—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (a) a claim for personal injuries arises from a road traffic accident which occurred on or after 31st May 2021; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (b) rules 26.8, 26.10 or 26.11 do not apply to that claim,

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] the claimant must state in the claim form whether the amount which the claimant expects to recover as general damages for pain suffering and loss of amenity is—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (i) not more than £5,000; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (ii) more than £5,000.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (3AA) Where—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (a) a claim for personal injuries arises from a road traffic accident; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (b) rule 26.10 applies to that claim, the claimant must state in the claim form whether the amount which the claimant expects to recover as general damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenity is—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (i) not more than £1,000; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (ii) more than £1,000.”.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (3B) ‘Road traffic accident’ has the meaning ascribed to it by rule 26.9(3).

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (4) Where a tenant of residential premises, or a contract-holder of an occupation contract of a dwelling under section 7 of the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016, claims an order against a landlord requiring the landlord to carry out repairs or other work, the claimant must also state in the claim form—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (a)whether the estimated costs of those repairs or other work is—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (i)not more than £1,000; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (ii)more than £1,000; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (b)whether the value of any other claim for damages is—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (i)not more than £1,000; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (ii)more than £1,000.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (5) If the claim form is to be issued in the High Court it must, where this rule applies—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (a)state that the claimant expects to recover more than £100,000;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (b)state that some other enactment permits or requires the claim to be brought in the High Court and specify that enactment;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (c)if the claim is for personal injuries, state that the claimant expects to recover £50,000 or more; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (d)state that the claim is to proceed in one of the specialist High Court lists and state which list.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (6) When calculating how much the claimant expects to recover, the claimant must disregard any possibility—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (a)that the court may make an award of—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (i)interest;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (ii)costs;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (b)that the court may make a finding of contributory negligence;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (c)that the defendant may make a counterclaim or that the defence may include a set-off; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (d)that the defendant may (under section 6 of the Social Security (Recovery of Benefits Act 1997) be liable to pay direct to the Secretary of State part of any award of money made by the court to the claimant against the defendant.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.3] (7) The statement of value in the claim form does not limit the power of the court to give judgment for an amount which it finds the claimant is entitled to.

## Contents of the particulars of claim

## 16.4

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (1) Particulars of claim must include—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (a)a concise statement of the facts on which the claimant relies;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (b)if the claimant is seeking interest, a statement to that effect and the details set out in paragraph (2);

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (c)if the claimant is seeking aggravated damages(GL) or exemplary damages(GL), a statement to that effect and the grounds for claiming them;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (d)if the claimant is seeking provisional damages, a statement to that effect and the grounds for claiming them; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (e)such other matters as may be set out in a practice direction.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (2) If the claimant is seeking interest they must—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (a)state whether they are doing so—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (i)under the terms of a contract;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (ii)under an enactment and, if so, which; or

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (iii)on some other basis and, if so, what that basis is; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (b)if the claim is for a specified amount of money, state—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (i)the percentage rate at which interest is claimed;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (ii)the date from which it is claimed;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (iii)the date to which it is calculated, which must not be later than the date on which the claim form is issued;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (iv)the total amount of interest claimed to the date of calculation; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (v)the daily rate at which interest accrues after that date.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.4] (Part 22 requires particulars of claim to be verified by a statement of truth).

## Content of defence

## 16.5

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (1) In the defence, the defendant must deal with every allegation in the particulars of claim, stating—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (a)which of the allegations are denied;

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (b)which allegations they are unable to admit or deny, but which they require the claimant to prove; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (c)which allegations they admit.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (2) Where the defendant denies an allegation—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (a)they must state their reasons for doing so; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (b)if they intend to put forward a different version of events from that given by the claimant, they must state their own version.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (3) If a defendant—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (a)fails to deal with an allegation; but

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (b)sets out in the defence the nature of their case in relation to the issue to which that allegation is relevant,

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] the claimant is required to prove the allegation.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (4) Where the claim includes a money claim, the claimant must prove any allegation relating to the amount of money claimed, unless the defendant expressly admits the allegation.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (5) Subject to paragraphs (3) and (4), a defendant who fails to deal with an allegation shall be taken to admit that allegation.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (6) If the defendant disputes the claimant’s statement of value under rule 16.3 they must—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (a)state why they dispute it; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (b)if they are able, give their own statement of the value of the claim.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (7) If the defendant is defending in a representative capacity, they must state what that capacity is.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (8) If the defendant has not filed an acknowledgment of service under Part 10, they must give an address for service.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (Part 22 requires a defence to be verified by a statement of truth.)

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.5] (Rule 6.23 makes provision in relation to addresses for service.)

## Defence of set-off

## 16.6 Where a defendant—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.6 Where a defendant—] (a)contends that they are entitled to money from the claimant; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.6 Where a defendant—] (b)relies on this as a defence to the whole or part of the claim,

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.6 Where a defendant—] the contention may be included in the defence and set off against the claim, whether or not it is also an additional claim.

## Reply to defence

## 16.7

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.7] (1) If a claimant does not file a reply to the defence, the defendant must prove the matters raised in the defence.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.7] (2) If a claimant—

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.7] (a)files a reply to a defence; but

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.7] (b)fails to deal with a matter raised in the defence,

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.7] the defendant must prove that matter even though it is not dealt with in the reply.

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.7] (Part 22 requires a reply to be verified by a statement of truth.)

## Court’s power to dispense with statements of case

## 16.8 If a claim form has been –

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.8 If a claim form has been –] (a) issued in accordance with rule 7.2; and

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.8 If a claim form has been –] (b) served in accordance with rule 7.5,

[PART 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 16.8 If a claim form has been –] the court may make an order that the claim will continue without any other statement of case.
